Curriculum › Year 3

Year 3: what your child practises

In Year 3, Sharpwise has 30 topics in maths and 13 topics in English. Each one is below in plain words, with ideas to try at home.

Year 3 topics follow the National Curriculum for England. This page is made from the game's own list of topics, so it changes when the game does.

Play Sharpwise

Maths in Year 3

30 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Number: number and place value

Count in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s
Count in 4s, 8s, 50s, 100s; 10 or 100 more or less
Hundreds, Tens and Ones
What each digit is worth, and splitting a number into hundreds, tens and ones
Compare and Order to 1,000
Compare and order numbers to 1,000
Number Line to 1,000
Identify, represent and estimate numbers
Numbers to 1,000 in Words
Read and write numbers to 1,000 in numerals and words

Try at home:

  • Count stairs, spoons or steps together, then count backwards, and stop to ask what comes next.
  • Make numbers from pairs of playing cards and ask which digit stands for tens and which for ones.
  • Put two heaps of socks or coins side by side and ask which has more, and by how many.
  • Chalk a number line on the path and hop along it, asking where a number sits between two others.

Number: addition and subtraction

Mental Adding and Subtracting
3-digit number and 1s, 10s, 100s mentally
Column Adding and Subtracting
Columnar addition and subtraction to 3 digits
Estimate and Check
Estimate an answer, then check it by working backwards
Missing Numbers to 1,000
Missing number problems
Adding and Subtracting Problems
One- and two-step problems within 1,000

Try at home:

  • Add the prices of two snacks in your head, then take one away to check the answer.
  • Lay out 10 spoons and ask how many more make 10.

Number: multiplication and division

3, 4 and 8 Times Tables
3, 4 and 8 tables, × and ÷
3× table
3 times table
4× table
4 times table
8× table
8 times table
2-Digit × 1-Digit
2-digit × 1-digit, related facts
Times-as-Many Problems
Scaling and correspondence problems

Try at home:

  • Set out egg boxes or muffin trays and count the rows and columns to find the lots of.
  • Add the prices of two snacks in your head, then take one away to check the answer.

Number: fractions

Counting in Tenths
Count in tenths, ÷ 10
Fractions of Amounts
Unit and non-unit fractions of a set
Fractions on a Number Line
Fractions as numbers on a line
Equivalent Fractions
Equivalent fractions with diagrams
Adding and Subtracting Fractions
Add and subtract, same denominator, within one whole
Compare and Order Fractions
Compare and order unit and same-denominator fractions

Try at home:

  • Cut a pizza or an apple into equal parts and ask for one half, one quarter or three quarters.
  • Chalk a number line on the path and hop along it, asking where a number sits between two others.
  • Put two heaps of socks or coins side by side and ask which has more, and by how many.

Measurement

Length, Mass and Capacity
Measure, compare, add and subtract lengths, mass, capacity
Perimeter
Perimeter of simple 2-D shapes
Money and Change
Add and subtract money, give change, £ and p
Time to the Minute
Time to the minute, am/pm, 12- and 24-hour clocks
Roman Numerals to XII
Roman numerals I to XII
Calendar and Durations
Seconds, days in months and years, compare durations

Try at home:

  • Compare a cup, a jug and a bowl: which holds more? Use a ruler or shoe-lengths to measure the table.
  • Let your child pay with real coins at the shop and work out the change together.
  • Ask what the clock will say in half an hour, then check when the time comes.

Geometry: properties of shapes

Right Angles and Lines
Right angles, turns, horizontal, vertical, parallel and perpendicular lines

Try at home:

  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

Statistics

Bar Charts and Pictograms
Scaled bar charts and pictograms, one- and two-step questions

Try at home:

  • Tally the cars passing the window or the colours of socks, then say which has most and fewest.

English in Year 3

13 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Writing: transcription (spelling)

Year 3–4 Word List
Words often misspelt, words 1–50
More Prefixes
Further prefixes dis–, mis–, re–, sub–, inter–, super–, anti–, auto–
Suffixes -ly and -ation
The suffixes -ly (and its exceptions) and -ation
Doubling Letters
Doubling the last consonant when the last syllable is stressed (forgetting, gardening)
Tricky Sounds
The /ɪ/ sound spelt y (myth) and the /ʌ/ sound spelt ou (young)
Homophones, Part 1
Further homophones and near-homophones, accept/except to knot/not
Dictionary Order
Use the first 2 or 3 letters of a word to check its spelling in a dictionary
Dictation
Write from memory simple sentences, dictated by the teacher, that include words and punctuation taught so far

Try at home:

  • Choose three words a night: look, cover, write, check, and then say what makes each one tricky.
  • Say a word slowly, sound by sound, and ask your child to blend the sounds back into the word.

Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation

A or An
a or an according to whether the next word begins with a consonant or a vowel
Word Families
Word families based on common words, showing how words are related in form and meaning
Time, Place and Cause
Conjunctions, adverbs and prepositions to express time, place and cause
Has Gone or Went
The present perfect form of verbs in contrast to the past tense
Inverted Commas
Introduction to inverted commas to punctuate direct speech

Try at home:

  • Look at a favourite book together and spot the full stops, question marks and describing words.
